video_title: Spurs vs Suns Preseason Postgame Press Conferences: Mitch Johnson and Stephon Castle

quotes.speaker: Mitch Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mitch Johnson on the need for better transition defense
quotes.excerpt: it's just transition defense. It's making passes and playing the right way and all the things that we know.
quotes.quote: Just a couple of possessions that were not too deeply layered or complex, and it's just transition defense. It's making passes and playing the right way and all the things that we know. So, just a reminder again, not trying to overreact or be ridiculous, but we need to play to the identity and style of play and to the fundamentals that we are fully aware of that we're supposed to.
quotes.social_post: Mitch Johnson says the Spurs need to focus on transition defense and playing to their identity. He notes they need to get back to the fundamentals they are fully aware of.

quotes.speaker: Mitch Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mitch Johnson provides injury update on Devin Vassell
quotes.excerpt: I don't know any details. I just believe I think there's one time, I don't know if it was a contest or rotation, but he stepped on I believe it was Devin's foot.
quotes.quote: I don't know any details. I just believe I think there's one time, I don't know if it was a contest or rotation, but he stepped on I believe it was Devin's foot. And so hopefully he's okay, but yeah, I'm not quite sure.
quotes.social_post: Mitch Johnson provided a brief update on Devin Vassell after he appeared to step on a foot during the game. Johnson says he does not know the details yet but hopes he is okay.

quotes.speaker: Mitch Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mitch Johnson on the team's growth and maturity
quotes.excerpt: that's a maturity and a growth opportunity for us to not let something like that trick us.
quotes.quote: The numbers may lie sometimes, and that's how good those guys are. And so that's a maturity and a growth opportunity for us to not let something like that trick us.
quotes.social_post: Mitch Johnson on the Spurs team maturity: The numbers may lie sometimes and that is a growth opportunity for us to not let something like that trick us.

quotes.speaker: Mitch Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mitch Johnson on the development of young players
quotes.excerpt: every time they get to get on the court and see it, feel it, learn from it, positive reinforcement, learning opportunities are moments, it's great.
quotes.quote: It's kind of like when your kids start school, every day they get to go, something good will happen. If it doesn't go well, it's still good. So just every time they get to get on the court and see it, feel it, learn from it, positive reinforcement, learning opportunities are moments, it's great. They put their energy in the right spots and really been a pleasure to have around.
quotes.social_post: Mitch Johnson compares the development of his young players to kids starting school, noting that every time they get on the court it is a learning opportunity.

quotes.speaker: Mitch Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mitch Johnson on balancing Stephon Castle's playmaking duties
quotes.excerpt: I think so, but it's got to be a balance. He still got to set screens, he still got to put pressure on the rim.
quotes.quote: I think so, but it's got to be a balance. He still got to set screens, he still got to put pressure on the rim. I mean, I think he has so many opportunities to do that and the gravity that he creates, but yeah, we still have to balance all that stuff out as a team.
quotes.social_post: Mitch Johnson on balancing Stephon Castle's playmaking: He still has to set screens and put pressure on the rim. We have to balance all that stuff out as a team.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Castle
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle on the team's need to set a tone
quotes.excerpt: I think just setting the tone earlier. I think the way we, I wouldn't say the way we approach the game, because I feel like we all have the right mindset, the right approach, but I think just setting the tone defensively with our physicality and not letting them get so comfortable early.
quotes.quote: I think just setting the tone earlier. I think the way we, I wouldn't say the way we approach the game, because I feel like we all have the right mindset, the right approach, but I think just setting the tone defensively with our physicality and not letting them get so comfortable early. We weren't ourselves in that part of the game and that was mainly his message.
quotes.social_post: Stephon Castle says the Spurs need to set the tone defensively with more physicality early in games. He admitted they were not themselves in that part of the game.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Castle
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle on the motivation for preseason games
quotes.excerpt: the motivation is, I think just not skipping steps. I think just having that understanding of what it takes to get back to where we were.
quotes.quote: The motivation is, I think just not skipping steps. I think just having that understanding of what it takes to get back to where we were. Last year I don't think we skipped any steps from preseason, start of the season, whatever it was, and I feel like it kind of just shaped our identity and we started to figure it out really towards like end of December, mid-January is when we really started to figure it out. And I think we'll do the same thing here.
quotes.social_post: Stephon Castle on the Spurs preseason mindset: The motivation is not skipping steps. We have an understanding of what it takes to get back to where we were.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Castle
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle on his playmaking and court vision
quotes.excerpt: he's always been a great facilitator. You see it before well. I mean, his assist numbers, they could vary, honestly.
quotes.quote: It's been great. I mean, he's always been a great facilitator. You see it before well. I mean, his assist numbers, they could vary, honestly. It's just the way he sees the floor, the way teams guard him, he gets a different look every single game. So just knowing him, he's going to make the right read for that possession and we want him to be default aggressive in all those situations, but I think just the way that he sees the floor, it forces team to guard him a certain way.
quotes.social_post: Stephon Castle discusses the team's playmaking approach, noting that they want the primary ball handlers to be default aggressive in all situations.
